sections.label: Healthcare Services Bill replacing PHMCA
sections.summary: The Ministry introduces the Healthcare Services Bill to replace the PHMCA, providing flexible licensing and stronger patient safety safeguards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Taking into consideration the above issues with the changes that are needed in the evolving healthcare landscape that I have mentioned, it is timely that the Ministry is now introducing the Healthcare Services Bill to replace the existing PHMCA, so as to have better levers to regulate the safety and care provided by the existing, and also the evolving and newer, healthcare services providers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: First, to provide greater flexibility and modularity in licensing, to enable the development of new care models that centre around patient needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Second, to better protect patient safety and welfare by strengthening licensee governance and also introducing additional safeguards.

sections.label: Licensing non-premises-based healthcare services
sections.summary: The Bill introduces licensing requirements for non-premises-based services such as telemedicine, emergency ambulances, cell, tissue and gene therapy and clinical genetic testing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In addition, however, the Bill will introduce licensing requirements for certain non-premises-based services, such as telemedicine, emergency ambulances, and new specialised services, such as cell, tissue and gene therapy and clinical genetic testing.

sections.label: Exemptions for government entities
sections.summary: Government entities such as SAF medical centres and SCDF ambulances are exempted from the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Government entities, such as the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) medical centres and Singapore Civil Defence Forces (SCDF) ambulances, are exempted from this Bill.

sections.label: Services-based licensing framework
sections.summary: Part 2 of the Bill introduces a services-based licensing framework, moving away from the current premises-based framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As we transit into the Healthcare Services Act, we will move away from the current premises-based licensing framework, which, as I have mentioned at the outset, is a lot more rigid and inflexible, confined only to one licence per premises and also limited to those in physical brick-and-mortar premises.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Hence, Part 2 of the Bill introduces a services-based licensing framework which is more flexible and also more modular.

sections.label: Director's licence grant factors
sections.summary: Under clause 11, the Director of Medical Services must consider multiple factors in deciding whether to grant or renew a licence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The strengthening starts first from our licensing regime and, under clause 11 of the Bill, the Director of Medical Services, who is defined as the "Director", will be required to consider multiple factors in deciding whether to grant or to renew a licence.

sections.label: Employment restrictions on licensees
sections.summary: Clause 28 imposes employment restrictions on certain licensees, prohibiting employment of individuals convicted of prescribed egregious offences and requiring staff screening.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Therefore, this Bill introduces safeguards in this area at clause 28 to impose employment restrictions on certain licensees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Such licensees will be prohibited from employing any individual convicted of prescribed egregious criminal offences involving violent acts, and must provide the information of all prospective staff to the Ministry for screening with the Criminal Records Office.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Employers who wish to employ past offenders of prescribed offences in the appropriate case may apply to seek the approval of the Director, who will consider each such case on its own merits.

sections.label: Patient information measures
sections.summary: The Bill introduces measures to ensure patients are well-informed and not misled by errant healthcare providers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Next, the Bill will also introduce a number of measures to ensure that patients are well-informed and are aware and not misled by errant healthcare providers.

sections.label: Step-in care arrangements
sections.summary: Rules and powers will be introduced for step-in arrangements to ensure patient safety and continuity of care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we will put in place rules and powers to ensure the safety and continuity of care for patients through the introduction of "step-in" arrangements.

sections.label: Licensee accountability and sanctions
sections.summary: The Bill ensures licensee accountability by broadening regulatory sanctions and strengthening the regulatory toolkit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Bill will also ensure licensee accountability by broadening our range of regulatory sanctions and strengthening our regulatory toolkit.

sections.label: Phased implementation of Bill
sections.summary: MOH intends a phased implementation from early 2021 to end 2022, in three phases, starting with PHMCA laboratory licensees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: MOH intends to take a phased approach on the Bill, targeted to be from early 2021 through to the end of 2022 – a phased, graduated implementation of the regime under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Regulation of licensable healthcare services will be effected, therefore, in three phases, so that providers will be given sufficient time to understand the regulations and also, in some cases, to ramp up its own resources to meet the relevant regulatory requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The first phase will bring PHMCA laboratory licensees under the Bill’s regulatory regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In the third and final phase, hospital and long-term care services, as well as other new licensable services, will be regulated by the Bill.

sections.label: Modular licensing framework
sections.summary: The Bill changes from fixed-type licensing based on physical premises to a modular framework customisable by services provided.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As the Senior Minister of State has just elaborated, a key feature of this Bill is the change from the current fixed-type licensing framework, which is based on physical premises, to a framework which is modular, with the flexibility of customisation based on the services provided.

sections.label: Help for existing providers
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry will help existing medical service providers, especially smaller players, convert to the new regime.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As with any major transition, the process of porting over will involve some work for current licensees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, my first question is to ask if the Ministry would share how it will help existing medical service providers, especially the smaller players, with this conversion to the new licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Will the overall licensing revenue be increased with the enactment of the Bill?

sections.label: Bill omits NEHR framework
sections.summary: The Bill omits setting out the legal framework for a National Electronic Health Record system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last, it should be remarked that one notable aspect of this Bill is what it omits, and the elephant in the room is that the setting out of the legal framework for a National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) system is not included in this Bill.

sections.label: Technical assistance and Bill support
sections.summary: The speaker asks what technical assistance, funding and resources are available, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What kind of technical assistance, funding and resources are available to help them set up secure systems and maintain their digital systems?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I look forward to these clarifications and I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Thus, it is, indeed, time to review and update to ensure patient safety through licensure, provision of more safeguards and, of course, keeping abreast of the new healthcare landscape and modalities we have today.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The migration from a premises-based to a service-based model makes sense because we are trying to integrate a lot of our healthcare services.

sections.label: Costs of service-based licencing
sections.summary: The speaker asks what framework or formula will govern conversion costs and whether the hike will be reasonable.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Seventh, with the move from premises-based to service-based licencing, many are concerned with the rise in the costs they have to pay.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: What will be the framework or formula for this conversion and can the Minister ensure that the hike will be within reasonable limits?

sections.label: Clause 5 government healthcare exemption
sections.summary: Clause 5 states the Bill does not apply to healthcare services provided by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 5 states that the Bill does not apply to any healthcare service provided by the Government.

sections.label: Private ambulance services phase 2
sections.summary: The Senior Minister of State said private ambulance services would come under phase 2 of implementation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I was puzzled because I had previously raised concerns about the private ambulance services used by consumers and also the feedback from residents about poor quality service and also hidden charges not being feasible at the time of booking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But I believe that, if I heard the Senior Minister of State correctly, he mentioned that this would come under phase 2 of the implementation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Related to that, in last year's Committee of Supply when I raised this issue, the Senior Minister of State mentioned about price transparency that the Healthcare Services Bill would include this issue in its regulation and it would mandate the publication of common fees charged, as well as give more transparency to the bill components to be paid by consumers so that they would know upfront what those costs would be.

sections.label: Opting out of NEHR
sections.summary: The Ministry said patients concerned about confidentiality could possibly opt out of having data input into NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In responding to the feedback, the Ministry stated that patients concerned about the confidentiality of their medical data could possibly opt out of having their data inputed into NEHR by healthcare service providers.

sections.label: Nationwide healthcare records database
sections.summary: The mandatory nationwide healthcare records database will ensure continuity of care for patients across service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The mandatory nationwide healthcare records database will also ensure continuity of care for patients across service providers.

sections.label: NEHR data access rules
sections.summary: NEHR data can only be accessed for healthcare services or with Government approval, and third parties need patient permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, NEHR data can only be accessed for the provision of healthcare services, or with the approval of the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third parties, such as employers and insurance providers, cannot access the data unless the patient permits.

sections.label: Ministry step-in provisions
sections.summary: Step-in provisions let the Ministry take over operations of providers at risk of insolvency or unable to resolve patient safety concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The step-in provisions allow the Ministry to take over the operations of providers at the risk of insolvency, or who are unable to resolve systemic patient safety or welfare concerns.

sections.label: Services-based licensing framework support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the services-based licensing framework as it addresses limits of the PHMCA, which regulates only brick-and-mortar facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, I support the proposed services-based licensing framework, as it addresses the limitations of the current PHMCA, which only regulates services provided at brick-and-mortar healthcare facilities.

sections.label: New licensing framework and costs
sections.summary: The new licensing framework lets providers modularise licences by services rather than premises, but the speaker is concerned about licensing costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill’s new licensing framework is, therefore, timely as it will provide healthcare providers with the flexibility to "modularise" and apply for relevant licences based on the services that they provide, rather than be confined to a physical premises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, while the new framework provides much needed flexibility, I am concerned with the corresponding licensing costs – how will they be impacted under the new regulatory regime?

sections.label: Telemedicine sandbox liability scope
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the telemedicine regulatory sandbox's scope will be wide enough to provide a sandbox liability regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Will the scope of the telemedicine regulatory sandbox be wide enough to provide a sandbox liability regime?

sections.label: GP clinics regulatory impact
sections.summary: Asks how the new regulatory requirement will affect the operations of 1,700 GP clinics, many with a small team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How will this new regulatory requirement affect the operations of our 1,700 GP clinics, many of which might just be a small team of one doctor and a few clinical assistants?

sections.label: Private ambulance service licensing
sections.summary: Private ambulance services must classify as Emergency Ambulance Services or Medical Transport Services and meet respective requirements, with questions on supply and worsening patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, private ambulance services will have to classify themselves either as Emergency Ambulance Services or Medical Transport Services and comply with the respective sets of requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Medical transport ambulances, for example, will not be allowed to be fitted with sirens and blinkers, while emergency ambulance services will be held to higher standards of emergency care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While I commend the Ministry's ongoing efforts to provide a voluntary accreditation scheme to facilitate a seamless transition to the new licensing framework, how will the introduction of the new regulation affect the supply of ambulance services in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What will happen in cases where someone calls for a medical transport service, but the patient’s condition worsens along the way and it becomes an emergency?

sections.label: Healthcare licensing cost and qualifications
sections.summary: Asks how services-based licensing affects operating cost, patient treatment by qualified persons, licence checks, and use of the title Dr.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is especially so with the growing number of elderly persons in our population which would increase the demand for certain services.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that the Bill would introduce a services-based licensing regime to replace the one that is premises-based licensing.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Overall, I hope the Minister can tell this House how these changes will impact on healthcare services in terms of operating cost, because, invariably, this cost may be passed on the consumers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the proliferation of new healthcare services, how do we ensure that patients are only treated by qualified persons?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Or if they are getting their blood drawn by someone who goes clinic to clinic, whose responsibility is it to check for a valid licence – the clinic or the patient?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask how the Ministry views someone who, for example, holds a doctorate in liberal arts but subsequently takes up, say, physiotherapy but uses his title Dr so and so.

sections.label: Services-based licensing regime objectives
sections.summary: Introduces services-based licensing for healthcare providers, strengthens patient safeguards, improves governance, and enhances regulatory powers including intervention in failing providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To introduce a services-based licensing regime for providers of healthcare services replacing the old premises-based licensing regime; to strengthen the safeguards for the safety and welfare of patients; to improve the governance requirements for providers of healthcare services; to enhance regulatory powers in relation to providers of healthcare services, including allowing intervention in failing providers in order to stabilise operations and ensure continued patient care.

sections.label: Private versus public hospital bills
sections.summary: A 2018 media report quoted LIA finding average private hospital bills rose 8% a year versus under 3% for public hospital bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A media report from late 2018 quoted the Life Insurance Association of Singapore (LIA), have found that average private hospital bills were increasing by 8% a year compared to less than 3% for public hospital bills, though I note that the 3% figure is still far higher than general inflation.

sections.label: MOH private fee benchmarks
sections.summary: From November 2018 MOH published non-mandatory private sector fee benchmarks, now covering 222 common surgical procedures comprising 85% of all procedures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In November 2018, MOH started publishing fee benchmarks for private sector professional fees, which are not mandatory caps, but which place some onus on healthcare service providers to justify their fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MOH now publishes information on 222 common surgical procedures like hip replacement and colonoscopy, comprising 85% of all procedures.

sections.label: Portugal C-section funding commission
sections.summary: Portugal created a national commission to monitor C-section rates and indexed hospital funding partly to C-section rates, per an OECD and European Commission report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, according to the "Health at a Glance: Europe 2018" report by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and European Commission, Portugal created a national commission to monitor C-section rates and indexed funding to hospitals partly to C-section rates.

sections.label: Day surgery cost savings
sections.summary: A 2016 review found costs of 11 common procedures would have been 14% higher without increased day surgery, and a Member asked about publishing data and tweaking funding models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The expansion of day surgery has helped achieve substantial savings...A 2016 review by the National Board of Health and Welfare showed that the costs of the 11 most common types of procedures would have been 14% higher if the share of day surgery had not increased between 2005 and 2013.” Sir, I would like to ask if the Government could consider publishing data on lower cost procedures at major healthcare service providers and perhaps even making tweaks to funding models to incentivise these lower cost approaches where relevant.

sections.label: Insurance billed for new pill
sections.summary: The company billed insurance $3,252 for the new pill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The company billed insurance $3,252 for the new pill.

sections.label: Drug stability testing study
sections.summary: A 2006 study of 122 drugs tested by the programme showed two-thirds were stable every time a lot was tested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A 2006 study of 122 drugs tested by the programme showed that two-thirds of them were stable every time a lot was tested.

sections.label: Allied health licensing under Bill
sections.summary: A Member notes that Allied Health, Non-Physician Healthcare, and Traditional, Complementary and Alternative medicine fall under the HCS Bill but will not be licensed for the time being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I do have some questions concerning the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that although Allied Health and Non-Physician Healthcare, Traditional, Complementary and Alternative medicine fall under the HCS Bill, they will not be licensed for the time being.

sections.label: Bill excludes government healthcare services
sections.summary: Part 1 of clause 5 states the Bill does not apply to and is not related to any healthcare service provided by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Next, I refer to Part 1 of clause 5 of this Bill which states that the Bill does not apply to and is not related to any healthcare service provided by the Government.

sections.label: NEHR mandatory contribution timeline
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOH plans to make NEHR core data contribution mandatory for licensees and for a timeline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These recommendations are targeted to be implemented fully in three years' time and I applaud the committee for the extensive review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, with these initiatives set in place, I seek clarification as to whether MOH has plans to introduce mandatory NEHR core data contribution by licensees and, if so, can the Minister provide a timeline so that private healthcare facilities may be better prepared in the eventuality that these recommendations are implemented?

sections.label: Pharmacy under two Acts
sections.summary: The same pharmacy is subject to two different Acts, the PHMCA for hospital patients and the Health Product Act for walk-in patients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although the type and level of services provided are similar, the same pharmacy is subjected to two different Acts, respectively, hospital patients which fall under the PHMCA, as compared to the walk-in patients which fall under the Health Product Act.

sections.label: Services-based flexible modular licensing
sections.summary: Moving from a premises-based fixed licensing model to a services-based flexible modular one will strengthen Government governance over the medical sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Moving from the current premises-based, fixed licensing model to a services-based, flexible modular one will enable our Government to strengthen its governance over the medical sector.

sections.label: Ensuring quality of diagnoses
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will ensure the quality of diagnoses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry ensure the quality of diagnoses?

sections.label: Remote prescriptions abuse risks
sections.summary: The passage asks whether remote prescriptions will be permitted and what the Ministry assesses the risks of abuse and fraud to be.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Will remote prescriptions be permitted and what is the Ministry’s assessment of the risks of abuse and fraud?

sections.label: Buyout loophole must be plugged
sections.summary: New companies may buy out or take over existing ones with the coveted terms, a loophole that must be plugged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In order to get around this constraint, new companies may buy out or take over existing ones with the coveted terms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is a loophole which must be plugged.

sections.label: Healthcare Services definition scope
sections.summary: Clause 3 defines Healthcare Services widely and includes services provided not for reward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Healthcare Services is defined under clause 3 quite widely and it also includes services provided not for reward.

sections.label: Unlicensed centres under PHMCA
sections.summary: It asks how many of these centres are not currently licensed under PHMCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If the intention is to include these corporations, how many of these centres are not currently licensed under PHMCA?

sections.label: Key appointment holder suitability
sections.summary: Clause 23(1)(a) requires a licensee to ensure every key appointment holder is, in the Director's opinion, suitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Clause 23(1)(a) of the Bill provides that a licensee must ensure that every key appointment holder of the licensee is, in the opinion of the Director, a suitable person to act in that capacity in relation to the licensee.

sections.label: Bill revenue-neutral for providers
sections.summary: The Ministry will not collect more revenue from existing providers, so the Bill is revenue-neutral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I further understand that the Ministry will not be collecting more revenue from existing providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Hence, this Bill is meant to be revenue-neutral.

sections.label: NEHR data and security concerns
sections.summary: It asks about preventive measures for erroneous diagnoses and concerns about database security and system failure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Going forward, all healthcare institutions, including laboratories, must input patient data into NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, if any physician were to arrive at an erroneous conclusion and make a wrong diagnosis, this may have an impact on subsequent consultations or any follow-ups by other medical practitioners referencing the patient's medical history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Minister share what preventive measures are in place to minimise such incidents?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, I am also concerned about the security of the database and potential system failure.

sections.label: Licensing by service kind
sections.summary: Licences under this Bill are based on the kind of services provided, not physical location.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Instead of licensing by physical location, the licences under this Bill are based on the kind of services provided.

sections.label: Healthcare cost inflation concern
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked how it will keep healthcare service costs down given enhanced regulation, citing 2018 healthcare cost inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Given enhanced regulation, how will the Ministry help to keep the costs of running healthcare services down?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is crucial as it was reported in June 2019 that healthcare cost inflation in Singapore in 2018 was 10 times that of the economic inflation rate.

sections.label: Step-in orders purpose
sections.summary: Clause 33(1) step-in orders prevent disruption in patient care from financial matters, licence loss, or acts against public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: From clause 33(1), step-in orders are used to prevent a disruption in care of the patients due to financial matters, such as insolvency, lack of licence after a suspension or revocation, or where the licensee carries out things against the public interest or in contravention of the Act.

sections.label: Assistance for entry and inspection
sections.summary: Clause 41(6) requires any person present at premises to render assistance and cooperation for entry, inspection and investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 41(6) of the Bill did not appear in the Act and requires any person present at any premises to render all necessary assistance and cooperation for entry, inspection, investigation.

sections.label: Bill expands healthcare regulation
sections.summary: The Bill expands healthcare regulation through a modular system not bound by locale, adapting to technology and protecting public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As healthcare services impact us directly, a good healthcare network is an important line of defence for the people of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill changes the landscape and expands the horizon of the regulation of healthcare services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: No longer bound by locale, this modular system provides more flexibility to adapt to rapidly-changing technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Besides ensuring that our regulatory regime is able to cope with and harness the benefits of technology, this Bill also puts in place measures to protect public interest in the provision of healthcare.

sections.label: Social services not regulated
sections.summary: Services predominantly social in nature, including Senior Activity Centres, will not be regulated under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Our primary focus as we implement the Bill is on services that provide clinical care for a condition or a disease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I think Mr Murali Pillai mentioned senior care centres, for instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These entities, including Senior Activity Centres, provide services which are predominantly social in nature and they will, to that extent, not be regulated under the Bill.

sections.label: Calibrated risk-based licensing approach
sections.summary: MOH will adopt a calibrated and risk-based approach to progressively license other healthcare services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, as to when these other services will be included, MOH will be adopting a calibrated and risk-based approach to progressively license healthcare services.

sections.label: Agents of principal medical providers
sections.summary: These agents act for principal medical providers and do not provide direct patient care, so they will not be licensed under this framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: They are agents of the principal medical providers and are not engaged in direct patient care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, they will not be licensed under this framework.

sections.label: Hospital pharmacy walk-in customers
sections.summary: A hospital pharmacy serving only in-hospital patients is covered by the hospital's licence; serving walk-in customers requires retail pharmacy standards under HPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If a pharmacy is part of a hospital and only serves in-hospital patients, then its licence will be part of the hospital's, the hospital being the primary licensee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Hence, I should clarify that the scenario that Ms Irene Quay contemplates occurs only when a hospital pharmacy also chooses to serve walk-in customers in addition to serving the hospital's patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That being the case, the pharmacy would be expected to abide by the retail pharmacy standards set out under HPA.

sections.label: Services newly regulated under Bill
sections.summary: Dr Chia Shi-Lu, Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Joan Pereira asked how telemedicine and ambulance services, first regulated under the Bill, will be regulated before rollout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu, Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Joan Pereira have asked about services that will be regulated for the first time under the Bill, in other words, not previously or hitherto regulated, but introduced for the first time under this Bill, and these include services like telemedicine and ambulance services, and asked how these services will be regulated prior to the rollout and implementation of this Bill.

sections.label: MOH Regulatory Sandbox telemedicine
sections.summary: MOH has set up the Regulatory Sandbox to work closely with telemedicine providers to co-develop service-specific regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On this score, MOH has set up the Regulatory Sandbox to work closely with telemedicine providers to co-develop service-specific regulations.

sections.label: Ambulance operators VAS licensing
sections.summary: Over 50% of private ambulance operators are on the VAS; ambulance services will be licensed in the second phase and VAS operators ported over as HCS Bill licensees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At present, more than 50% of private ambulance operators have come on board the VAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As such, ambulance services will be licensed in the second phase, as I mentioned at the opening speech, of implementation, and ambulance operators under VAS will be seamlessly ported over as licensees under the HCS Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: MOH will be working with the VAS ambulance operators to develop and publish an appropriate range of fees charged, so that consumers can have more transparency and can better make up their minds and have informed choices of the providers to use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We intend to publish those fees before these ambulance operators are phased in under the second phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And, in fact, we target to do so in the course of this year.

sections.label: Clause 48(7)(b) Minister appeals
sections.summary: Clause 48(7)(b) provides for appeals to the Minister and allows the Minister to vary or substitute the Director's decision as appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Clause 48(7) (b) of the Bill, which provides for appeals to the Minister, allows the Minister to vary, substitute the decision of the Director, as the case might be appropriate, upon the appeal.

sections.label: QACs under current PHMCA
sections.summary: QACs are already an existing requirement under the current PHMCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: QACs are already an existing requirement under the current PHMCA.

sections.label: CEC review of ethical cases
sections.summary: They review ethically-challenging cases and ensure ethical care and treatment, with a list of prescribed medical treatments requiring CEC review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: They review ethically-challenging cases and ensure that ethical care and treatment are provided in the context of the facts of that case and the treatment, modality or options that have been considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There will be a list of prescribed medical treatments that require CEC review, where the care management of patients is likely to be complex; where societal values could be either undermined or challenged; and where the values of the medical practitioners might be challenged as well.

sections.label: Step-in powers as last resort
sections.summary: Step-in powers will be activated sparingly and as a last resort, with licensees given written representation opportunity unless an urgent order is required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ultimately, of course, that is a multifaceted and dynamic assessment of the facts in each case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We would like to, however, assure the House that the step-in powers will be activated sparingly and as a measure of last resort for the specified licensees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Licensees will be given an opportunity to make written representations before the step-in order is activated, unless it is an extreme case where an expedited or urgent step-in order is required.

sections.label: Background checks for prospective staff
sections.summary: Mandated background checks are conducted by licensees on all prospective staff, and existing employees will not be affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Irene Quay's queries regarding the restriction on employment of certain individuals in long-stay settings, the mandated background checks are to be conducted by licensees on all prospective staff, and existing employees will not be affected.

sections.label: Cybersecurity guidelines for healthcare services
sections.summary: This includes developing customised cybersecurity guidelines and supporting smaller healthcare providers, with details released in the first half of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This will no doubt include developing cybersecurity guidelines specific and customised to the various healthcare services and exploring efforts to better support smaller healthcare providers as they take steps to improve their cyber and data security positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will be engaging the licensees on this effort and will be releasing more details on this in the first half of 2020.

sections.label: Mandatory NEHR contribution deferred
sections.summary: The mandatory contribution to NEHR has been deferred until all enhancements are completed and the system is assessed as sufficiently robust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As such, as has been announced previously, the mandatory contribution to NEHR has been deferred until all the enhancements have been completed, and we are satisfied that the system is assessed to be sufficiently robust.

sections.label: Existing prohibited names carried over
sections.summary: Entities already using prohibited names may continue if licensee and ownership do not change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will consider these in implementing the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I would add to Ms Joan Pereira's point that should an entity today already be using one of these otherwise prohibited names, if the licensee does not change, the ownership does not change, and it is simply carried over into the new Bill, we will be prepared to allow them to continue using the name.

sections.label: Insurance in long-term care
sections.summary: Insurance role in long-term care is enhanced, including CareShield Life, Integrated Shield Plan rider requirements and published fee benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Looking ahead, we are also enhancing the role of insurance in long-term care, such as with the launch of CareShield Life from mid-2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These include requirements under Integrated Shield Plan insurers for new rider plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have also developed and published fee benchmarks, as Mr Leon Perera himself noted, for private sector professional fees for common surgical procedures.

sections.label: Price transparency and Service Review Committee
sections.summary: The Bill requires display of common charges, financial counselling, bill itemisation, and establishes a Service Review Committee for high-cost services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Bill supports this by seeking to improve price transparency, such as requiring licensees to display common charges; by mandating financial counselling and itemisation of bills for certain settings, such as procedures conducted by hospitals or specialist clinics; and also establishing the Service Review Committee to monitor utilisation and clinical outcomes of certain high-cost and more complex services, such as proton beam therapy, for example, to ensure that not just is the care provided appropriate but it is also cost-effective, to take into account and to assuage Mr Leon Perera's concern that not all high cost procedures are necessarily good quality procedures and, perhaps, not all good quality procedures are also at the same cost-effective level.

sections.label: Transition from PHMCA to HCS Bill
sections.summary: MOH will guide licensees through transition, swapping PHMCA licences for equivalent ones without applications or additional fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On Dr Chia Shi-Lu and Mr Christopher de Souza’s query on how we will help providers, specifically the smaller ones, transition from the current PHMCA to the future HCS Bill, let me assure the House that MOH will support and guide all licensees to ensure a seamless transition to the new licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This will be done at each implementation phase, where PHMCA licences will be swapped out for equivalent licences under this Bill, without the need for existing licensees to file any applications or pay additional fees.

sections.label: No aggregate licensing fee increase
sections.summary: MOH states it would not collect more licensing fees in aggregate under the new regime than today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: MOH would not, under this new regime, overall be collecting more licensing fees on an aggregate basis, compared to the position today.

sections.label: Most providers see no fee increase
sections.summary: Preliminary assessment shows more than 95% of existing providers will see no change or a decrease in fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In fact, based on our preliminary assessment as we map the services across to the new HCS Bill requirements, based on our assessment, more than 95% of existing providers today will see either no change or a decrease in the amount of fees that they will have to pay.

sections.label: Mitigation for higher provider fees
sections.summary: MOH will support existing providers facing higher fees with mitigation measures, including phasing the increase over three licensing renewal cycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For existing providers facing higher fees, MOH will put in mitigation measures to support the transition and this would include implementing the increase gradually over three licensing renewal cycles.
